title: Attention via per-head sgemm; band-limit sliding layers
description: lla_attention: QK^T and PV as cblas_sgemm per head (split-qkv already lays each head out as a contiguous [L x hd] block). On sliding layers only the |i-j|<=window band is needed; skip the rest. Keep lla_scores/lla_weighted_sum callable for the kernel tests.
acceptance_criteria: tensors_test layer goldens pass (1e-4 abs, 5e-5 rel last layer); readme/presets answers unchanged; scale bench: 512 tokens under 1.2 s, ~linear in L

title: Latency: attention kernel, batched encoder, constrained decoding
description: One noul question takes 182 ms at 55 tokens and 4.8 s at 512 tokens. The only O(L^2) term is attention, and lla_scores / the PV loop in native/laya_kernels.c are scalar loops with a double accumulator while every other matmul goes through cblas_sgemm. Per-head sgemm does the same work ~90x faster (0.04 s vs 3.9 s at L=512 over 30 layers). After that the encoder is weight-GEMM bound and batching a call's questions pays. Then port GLiNER2's constrained multi-task decoder (torch-free) as a workflow/API extension so answers across questions are consistent.

title: Constrained multi-question decoding (port of gliner2.classification)
description: Port gliner2/classification/{constraints,candidates}.py and decoding/ (torch-free): constraint AST as EDN (implies, iff, excludes, not, all-of, any-of, exactly-one-of, at-least/at-most/exactly, at-level/min-level/max-level/between-level, any-selected), Kleene 3-valued evaluation, exact DFS with branch-and-bound, beam fallback, relax -> min-violations -> raise ladder. choice <-> single, score <-> ordinal, a set of nouls <-> multi. Consumes the per-question probability vectors system-one already computes. Workflows declare constraints; the API accepts them; answers without constraints stay byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria: unit tests for the evaluator and decoders incl. exact-vs-brute-force; email workflow with spam => not needs_reply; feasible/violations reported in the answer

title: Batch a call's questions through the encoder
description: system-one runs forward-row once per question; each pass re-reads 1.7 GB of weights. Stack the B rows into one [B*L x d] stream per layer so weights are read once, with per-row attention and masks. Rows have different L; pad to the max with the attention mask, or group by length.
acceptance_criteria: answers byte-identical to the unbatched path on the goldens; demo (4 questions) and email (5) measurably faster than 1x per question

title: Benchmark gliner2.5 on the 64-case set before deciding on a port
description: pip install gliner2[local]; classify_text with the same labels/instructions on the 64 cases from the Jev comparison. Decides whether a DeBERTa-v3 + Unigram tokenizer port to jolt is worth it (~1500 lines; one forward pass for all questions, 74M/194M params).
